beats.label: S1 · Demoted to Slough House
beats.text: River Cartwright is scapegoated for a Stansted training disaster and exiled to Slough House, MI5's dumping ground for failures under caustic boss Jackson Lamb.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the show's premise and the entire ensemble's shared humiliation.

beats.label: S1 · Hassan taken
beats.text: Far-right Sons of Albion abduct student Hassan Ahmed and threaten a livestreamed beheading; Slough House is quietly ordered to probe a linked journalist, Robert Hobden.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The case that pulls the team into the season's central conspiracy.

beats.label: S1 · Sid is shot
beats.text: An intruder chasing Hobden shoots Sid Baker in the head; Lamb realises the gunman was Slough House's own Jed Moody, sent by someone at Regent's Park.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First evidence that a senior MI5 figure is running an off-book op against them.

beats.label: S1 · Taverner's false flag
beats.text: Deputy DG Diana Taverner admits she engineered the kidnapping as a false-flag op, planting mole Alan Black in the cell to boost Pakistan ties and shame the far-right.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names Taverner as the season's true antagonist and the ongoing threat to Slough House.

beats.label: S1 · Plan collapses
beats.text: Curly unmasks and kills Black then flees with Hassan; Taverner moves to pin the botched operation on Slough House and coerces a colleague into testifying against Lamb.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the kidnapping into an existential threat to the whole team.

beats.label: S1 · Blackmail and rescue
beats.text: River recovers a photo of Taverner meeting Black, giving Lamb the leverage to force her hand; the team tracks Curly to a folly and saves Hassan, openly defying Regent's Park.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the mutual-blackmail stalemate between Lamb and Taverner that defines their future dynamic.

beats.label: S1 · Lamb killed Partner
beats.text: A flashback shows Lamb killed his old friend Charles Partner, then MI5's DG, on David Cartwright's orders after foreign blackmail. Roddy hints Sid Baker may still be alive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the Partner/Standish/David past that will drive later seasons; keeps Sid's fate live.

cliffhanger.text: Slough House survives via mutual blackmail with Taverner rather than any real victory. Sid's records have been quietly erased, hinting she may still be alive somewhere, and Standish has just learned that Lamb gave her old friend Charles Partner the gun he used to kill himself.
questions: Will Taverner strike back once the blackmail loses its bite?
Is Sid Baker really alive, and where has MI5 hidden her?
Can Standish stay loyal to Lamb after learning he shot Charles Partner?

characters.name: Jackson Lamb
characters.line: Slovenly, brutal boss of Slough House who protects his agents when Regent's Park comes for them.

characters.name: River Cartwright
characters.line: Ambitious young agent unfairly exiled after Stansted; grandson of MI5 legend David Cartwright.

characters.name: Catherine Standish
characters.line: Lamb's clean, recovering-alcoholic assistant who once served Partner and believes Lamb gave him the gun he used to kill himself.

characters.name: Diana Taverner
characters.line: MI5 Deputy DG whose false-flag scheme was exposed; held in check by Lamb's photo evidence.

characters.name: David Cartwright
characters.line: Retired MI5 grandee, River's grandfather, and the man who ordered Partner's execution.

characters.name: Sid Baker
characters.line: Slough House agent shot in the head chasing Hobden; her records have been erased, suggesting she may be alive.

characters.name: Roddy Ho
characters.line: Slough House's arrogant, socially oblivious hacker.

characters.name: Min Harper
characters.line: Slough House agent, mildly hapless, close with Louisa.

characters.name: Louisa Guy
characters.line: Slough House agent, sharper than her posting suggests, close with Min.

characters.name: James "Spider" Webb
characters.line: River's smug Regent's Park rival, exposed as having deliberately sabotaged him at Stansted for Taverner.

beats.label: S2 · Dickie Bough dies
beats.text: Ex-agent Dickie Bough spots a Cold War tormentor on the London streets, but collapses after being covertly poisoned. Lamb finds Bough's cryptic note reading 'cicada'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The trigger that pulls Lamb into a case Regent's Park had long dismissed as folklore.

beats.label: S2 · Cicadas were real
beats.text: KGB defector Nikolai Katinsky tells Lamb that Popov's programme of Russian sleepers in Britain was real, and Bough's killer matches Popov's associate Chernitsky.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes the season as an active Russian operation, not a Cold War ghost hunt.

beats.label: S2 · Pashkin secondment
beats.text: Min and Louisa are seconded to Webb to secure a covert London meeting with oligarch Arkady Pashkin, ostensibly the envoy of defector Ilya Nevsky.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the parallel op that turns out to be the real Russian plot.

beats.label: S2 · Min murdered
beats.text: Min tails Pashkin's team to an Edgware Road address; Piotr and Kyril run him down and stage his death as a drunken cycling accident. Louisa is devastated.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills a core team member and gives Louisa the grief that defines her going forward.

beats.label: S2 · The real sleeper
beats.text: River, undercover in Upshott, finds Chernitsky wiring a bomb at the airfield. Duncan Tropper's wife Alex reveals herself as the true sleeper and stuns River unconscious.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cicada programme's operational payoff and the twist that a plane strike is coming.

beats.label: S2 · The Glasshouse diversion
beats.text: The plane-bomb threat is a ruse; while London evacuates, Pashkin's team drains Nevsky's accounts. New agent Marcus Longridge saves Louisa on the roof, killing Pashkin.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the whole operation as a heist and confirms Nevsky's murder.

beats.label: S2 · Popov unmasked
beats.text: Lamb confronts Katinsky as Popov himself, whose old MI5 mole was Charles Partner. Katinsky shoots himself, Alex escapes, and the affair is buried as a 'security glitch'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Partner betrayal loop and re-establishes cover-up as MI5's default; Judd walks away stronger.

cliffhanger.text: The Popov conspiracy is officially buried as a routine security glitch, with Peter Judd emerging politically stronger from the cover-up. Katinsky is dead but Alex Tropper is allowed to return to her sleeper life, and the team quietly memorialises Min at St Leonard's without official recognition.
questions: What does Judd do with his new political leverage over MI5?
Will Alex Tropper's sleeper role stay buried forever?
Can Louisa function at Slough House now that Min is gone?

characters.name: Jackson Lamb
characters.line: Slough House boss, now confirmed as the Cold War veteran who once had to shoot his own colleague Partner.

characters.name: River Cartwright
characters.line: Slough House agent who ran the Upshott op; still restless to prove himself worthy of Regent's Park.

characters.name: Catherine Standish
characters.line: Lamb's assistant, still processing that her old hero Partner was a Soviet asset all along.

characters.name: Diana Taverner
characters.line: MI5 Deputy DG, complicit in the cover-up alongside Judd; still Slough House's institutional threat.

characters.name: Louisa Guy
characters.line: Slough House agent, hollowed out by Min's murder and denied any official memorial.

characters.name: Roddy Ho
characters.line: Slough House's hacker, still convinced he is the department's only real asset.

characters.name: Marcus Longridge
characters.line: New Slough House agent, ex-gambler exiled for his addiction; saved Louisa on the Glasshouse roof.

characters.name: Shirley Dander
characters.line: New Slough House agent, aggressive and prone to trouble, helping to run down Chernitsky.

characters.name: Peter Judd
characters.line: Home Secretary, politically bolstered by the buried Code September and increasingly powerful over MI5.

characters.name: David Cartwright
characters.line: Retired MI5 grandee, now confirmed as the man who ordered Lamb to kill Partner, still River's mentor.

beats.label: S3 · Standish taken
beats.text: An operative posing as an AA member abducts Standish, and River is ordered to steal the PM's MI5 vetting file from Regent's Park within the hour or she dies.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kicks off the season by putting Standish's life on a countdown clock.

beats.label: S3 · Chieftain's tiger team
beats.text: Lamb learns the kidnappers are Chieftain, a private firm hired by Home Secretary Judd as a 'tiger team' to expose MI5 weakness and justify privatising its security.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the political scheme underneath the kidnapping and reintroduces Judd as antagonist.

beats.label: S3 · Donovan goes rogue
beats.text: Chieftain operative Sean Donovan turns on his employers and moves Standish, secretly hunting those who killed his lover Alison Dunn to bury a file called 'Footprint'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the season from a hostage op into a personal vendetta with real stakes.

beats.label: S3 · Tearney's cover-up
beats.text: Footprint exposes DG Tearney's cover-up of a botched MI5 hacking trial; Dunn was murdered for planning to leak it, and Deputy DG Taverner was Donovan's secret source.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's true villain as the sitting DG, with Taverner playing both sides.

beats.label: S3 · Siege at the file facility
beats.text: Tearney sends Duffy's Chieftain strike team to kill everyone at the MI5 file facility. River, Louisa and Donovan hold them off; Alison's brother Ben dies helping find Footprint.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central set-piece where Slough House openly fights MI5's own attack team.

beats.label: S3 · Slough House wins the day
beats.text: Lamb saves Standish from a hit squad; Marcus and Shirley break the siege, Louisa kills Duffy, and Donovan sacrifices himself so River escapes carrying the Footprint file.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Marcus and Shirley as combat-capable field agents and gets the file into River's hands.

beats.label: S3 · Standish resigns, leaders fall
beats.text: Lamb reveals Partner was laying a trail to frame Standish as the Russian mole; shattered, she resigns. David burns Footprint, but River's leaked copy forces Tearney and Judd out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes MI5's two most powerful figures and knocks Standish out of Slough House.

cliffhanger.text: MI5's top two political operators, Tearney and Judd, have both been forced out by the Footprint leak. Standish has resigned in shock at her hero Partner's final betrayal, and River is quietly beginning to notice his grandfather David slipping into dementia.
questions: Who takes over as First Desk now that Tearney is gone?
Can Standish stay away from Slough House for long?
How far will David Cartwright's decline take him?

characters.name: Jackson Lamb
characters.line: Slough House boss, still the only person able to route around Regent's Park; now short one Standish.

characters.name: River Cartwright
characters.line: Slough House agent, quietly worried about David's memory and increasingly the department's field lead.

characters.name: Catherine Standish
characters.line: Just resigned after learning Partner was framing her all along; her future outside Slough House unclear.

characters.name: Diana Taverner
characters.line: MI5 Deputy DG who fed Donovan the Footprint tip; survived the leak with Tearney and Judd knocked out of the way.

characters.name: Louisa Guy
characters.line: Slough House agent, hardened field operator now; killed Duffy with a rock during the siege.

characters.name: Marcus Longridge
characters.line: Slough House agent, gambling addiction still simmering; proved himself in the file-facility fight.

characters.name: Shirley Dander
characters.line: Slough House agent, drug habit still simmering; broke the siege alongside Marcus.

characters.name: Roddy Ho
characters.line: Slough House hacker, still socially oblivious; crashed a bus through the Dunn house trying to help.

characters.name: David Cartwright
characters.line: Retired MI5 grandee, memory now visibly failing; burned Footprint to protect the Service.

characters.name: Molly Doran
characters.line: Regent's Park records overseer, guardian of MI5's paper history; refused to help River in the Park.

beats.label: S4 · Westacres bombing
beats.text: Suicide bomber Robert Winters kills scores at London's Westacres mall. Analyst Giti Rahman discovers Winters was a 'cold body' — a false identity created and stored by MI5 itself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The atrocity that points inward at MI5's own records rather than at any outside enemy.

beats.label: S4 · River dead, David gone
beats.text: A man claiming to be River arrives at David's house; a paranoid, failing David shoots him dead. Lamb identifies the body as River for the Dogs, then quietly hides David.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's inciting personal mystery and the reason River goes off-grid to France.

beats.label: S4 · Les Arbres
beats.text: River, alive, follows Bertrand's identity to Lavande in France and finds an estate, Les Arbres, where former CIA operative Frank Harkness has raised sons as trained assassins.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Harkness and his mercenary family, the season's real antagonists.

beats.label: S4 · Westacres was Yves' revenge
beats.text: Robert Winters is really Harkness' son Yves; Westacres was Yves' revenge against an abusive father. Harkness's employers now pressure him to silence David and bagman Sam Chapman.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ties the mall attack to the family conspiracy and puts David squarely in the crosshairs.

beats.label: S4 · David's original sin
beats.text: David admits he traded MI5 weapons, cash and cold-body IDs to Harkness thirty years ago for his own daughter — River's mother. Chapman is caught and killed by the assassin Patrice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rewrites David from grandee to the source of the entire threat; makes Harkness family.

beats.label: S4 · Slough House attacked
beats.text: Patrice traces David to Slough House and shoots his way in, killing Marcus. Shirley subdues him, but new agent JK Coe quietly executes Patrice before he can be taken alive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills Marcus, hardens Shirley, and reveals Coe's willingness to kill in cold blood.

beats.label: S4 · Harkness walks
beats.text: River captures Harkness, who negotiates his own release by threatening to expose MI5's long use of his assassins. David is committed to a care home against his will.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Leaves the season's villain uncontained and permanently sidelines David.

cliffhanger.text: Harkness walks free, protected by damning letters that would expose MI5's long-standing use of his mercenaries. Marcus is dead, David is committed against his will, and JK Coe has revealed a cold ruthlessness by executing Patrice at the end of the shootout.
questions: What does Harkness do with his freedom and his remaining sons?
How does Slough House hold together after Marcus's death?
Is JK Coe someone Lamb can actually control?

characters.name: Jackson Lamb
characters.line: Slough House boss, now down one agent and holding the whole Harkness cover on his own.

characters.name: River Cartwright
characters.line: Slough House agent who has just learned his own father is a rogue assassin, and committed his grandfather.

characters.name: Catherine Standish
characters.line: Ex-Slough House, still orbiting Lamb; sheltered David through the crisis.

characters.name: Louisa Guy
characters.line: Slough House agent, saved River from Harkness's grenade at the finale.

characters.name: Shirley Dander
characters.line: Slough House agent, second friend lost after Min; subdued Patrice but was stopped from finishing him.

characters.name: Roddy Ho
characters.line: Slough House hacker, still Roddy, now confined to a Slough House invaded by Patrice.

characters.name: JK Coe
characters.line: New Slough House agent with PTSD; shot Patrice execution-style after Shirley let him live.

characters.name: David Cartwright
characters.line: Committed to a care home against his will after admitting he traded state secrets for his daughter.

characters.name: Diana Taverner
characters.line: MI5 Deputy DG, has spent the season managing Whelan while positioning for the top job herself.

characters.name: Claude Whelan
characters.line: New First Desk of MI5, weak, blackmailable, leaning constantly on Taverner.

characters.name: Emma Flyte
characters.line: New commander of the Dogs, dogged and ethical; captured River and lost four Dogs to Patrice.

beats.label: S5 · Abbotsfield massacre
beats.text: Radicalised Gimball supporter Rob Trew guns down eleven in Abbotsfield, then is shot dead by an unseen sniper. Among the dead is a campaigner for London mayor Zafar Jaffrey.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the season with the first move in a coordinated attack whose shape only becomes clear later.

beats.label: S5 · Roddy honey-trapped
beats.text: Roddy's new girlfriend Tara is an enemy operative; Shirley saves him from a hit at his flat, but the attack was staged only to make MI5 believe he was the real target.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The deception that gives the terrorists their route into MI5's systems via Roddy.

beats.label: S5 · Destabilisation strategy
beats.text: Coe reads Abbotsfield, refinery sabotage, a zoo bombing and Roddy's compromise as steps of a destabilisation plan whose scripted next step is assassinating a populist leader.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment Slough House finally understands the pattern behind the incidents.

beats.label: S5 · Gimball dies by accident
beats.text: River and Coe, guarding populist Dennis Gimball's rally, accidentally cause his death when a scuffle drops a paint can onto his head. They steal his tape and hide their role.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fulfils the terrorists' scripted step by pure accident, and hands Lamb a piece of leverage he later cashes in.

beats.label: S5 · Libyan cell, Judd's arms
beats.text: The plot is a Libyan cell avenging Britain's role in Gaddafi's fall; the Abbotsfield weapon came from an arms firm Judd secretly advises, whose crate had gone conveniently missing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the enemy and drags Judd back into the frame as quiet collaborator.

beats.label: S5 · Embassy siege and ransom
beats.text: Tara seizes the Libyan embassy and MI5 pays a £100m ransom that flows into Judd's offshore account. Farouk still attacks Jaffrey's memorial, but Slough House stops him there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Judd's payday, and Slough House's decisive win that prevents the finale atrocity.

beats.label: S5 · Whelan out, Taverner in, Lamb's scar
beats.text: Lamb blackmails Whelan with Gimball's tape, forcing his resignation; Taverner becomes First Desk. Lamb's scarred foot confirms he was the Stasi torture victim from his own story.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reshuffles Regent's Park leadership and hints at a much darker Lamb backstory.

cliffhanger.text: Diana Taverner is finally First Desk and Peter Judd has emerged roughly £100m richer without any fingerprints on the payout. Slough House is saved but River is denied any promotion, and Lamb's scarred foot confirms the Stasi torture story he told his agents was his own.
questions: How does Slough House operate now that Taverner runs Regent's Park?
Will Judd's role in the £100m payout ever surface?
What else is Lamb still hiding about his own past?

characters.name: Jackson Lamb
characters.line: Slough House boss, has just quietly forced a DG's resignation and revealed himself as the Stasi torture victim in his own anecdote.

characters.name: River Cartwright
characters.line: Slough House agent, killed Sami to save Whelan and was denied any promotion for it.

characters.name: Catherine Standish
characters.line: Back around Slough House, helped Shirley uncover Tara's role and helped the Dogs take her alive.

characters.name: Shirley Dander
characters.line: Slough House agent, still grieving Marcus; saved Roddy and killed Kamal at the memorial.

characters.name: Roddy Ho
characters.line: Slough House hacker, unwittingly used as the Libyans' route in; freed by Taverner after Tara's capture.

characters.name: JK Coe
characters.line: Slough House agent, read the destabilisation pattern first and fatally stabbed Farouk at the memorial.

characters.name: Louisa Guy
characters.line: On a six-month mental health break at the season's opening; privately told River she plans to leave the Service.

characters.name: Diana Taverner
characters.line: The new First Desk of MI5, finally in the chair she has always wanted.

characters.name: Peter Judd
characters.line: Quietly £100m richer from the ransom he brokered, still politically untouched.

characters.name: David Cartwright
characters.line: Still in the care home; his offhand call about honey traps helped River see the final terrorist move.
